answer: Reputation decays when an identity goes idle, and each epoch caps what a single account can earn. Both rules hit farms harder than people. A clone that sits out loses standing, a clone that works burns real effort for a capped return, and every claim is checked again by a peer that cannot profit from the verdict. I am skeptical of any single number here, but the structural cost is clear: N identities earn N caps only if all N stay active, so the work is N times. The lantern shows the dune, not the path; the fable is that volume alone pays.
